sharedEditsNeeded: Media -vf (linear) CLI with output -ss: filters receive timestamps already shifted by the seek; native filters see the original timestamps. Needed for t on the linear path.
Media -filter_complex (graph) CLI with input -ss: the graph receives timestamps without the input seek offset native applies before filtering. Needed for t on the graph and stream paths.

Linear and frame-graph negotiators pass VideoShape without sampleAspectRatio to geometry(), and packages/avformat/src/actor-video/execute.ts runs graph.nodes[].configuration instead of the step returned by timedGeometry. Needed for sar and dar.
notes: Status partial: the scope lists sar, dar and t on every path; sar/dar are refused at parse time and t at plan time on linear/graph/stream for the shared reasons above. Everything accepted is byte-exact against native in the tests listed.
Variable use is detected by re-parsing each expression with that name removed from the constant table; unported functions and ^ are detected lexically after whitespace removal.

Time-independent expressions are evaluated at plan time with the negotiated geometry so their refusals surface before output on every path; t-dependent refusals can only surface at the offending frame.
No macOS run; no platform-gated case. No H.264/MP4 framecrc comparison (size-preserving).
Setup: Node 24.22.3 installed from nodejs.org (sandbox had 22.23.5); bootstrap 3m50s; baseline typecheck+lint+boundaries 1m04s and registry test 2.4s, all clean before changes.

Audit (pre-integration): on darwin-arm64 the option test failed ([17,7,2,12] for [17,7,4,10]) because native converts w=1/0 and w=3e9 to int with undefined behaviour, faulting on x86-64 but saturating and exiting 0 on arm64. The test now classifies those two cases explicitly: refused here on every platform, a signal asserted natively on x64 and exit 0 on arm64. With that change all 8 differential and 6 unit tests pass on darwin-arm64; the linux-x64 assertions are unchanged.
